A savings promotion has an expiry date: compare the interest over your whole holding period

Follow the rate calendar, separate deposits from interest and compare an introductory account with a constant-rate account under identical saving contributions.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Explore interest before and after a savings promotion ends

Interactive planning lab

Interest over the selected horizon · introductory account$285.86
Interest over the same horizon · constant-rate account$387.35
Introductory account minus constant-rate account-$101.49

Hypothetical savings accounts using nominal annual rates divided by twelve, with monthly crediting. At each month-end, interest is credited on the opening balance, then the equal deposit arrives. The introduction begins in month one and ends after the selected whole-month count; zero months means the ongoing rate applies immediately. The comparison uses its constant rate throughout. Rates apply to every modeled dollar with no cap or qualifying condition. No actual offer, daily accrual, transfer gap, fee, withdrawal, tax, bonus eligibility, deposit-insurance assessment or future change in the entered ongoing/comparison rate is modeled. These are nominal rate assumptions, not effective annual yields. All interest is retained and compounds.

The central idea

An annualized opening rate is only one part of the account’s cash-flow history. Compare the period it applies, the later rate and the money present during each month.

01

Translate the headline into a dated interest schedule

A promotional savings rate can be quoted as an annual rate even when it lasts only a few months. The first question is therefore when it starts and ends. The second is which rate applies afterward. A comparison using only the two opening rates leaves out most of the year when the introductory period is short.

The default illustration applies a hypothetical 5% nominal annual rate for three months, then 1.5% for the remaining months. The comparison account applies 3% throughout. Both begin with CAD 10,000 and receive CAD 500 at each month-end. There is no account transfer or second promotion after the first one ends.

The FCAC savings-account guide explains the distinction between introductory and later rates and the importance of checking account conditions. The percentages here are independently chosen assumptions, without a named bank or an available offer.

02

Separate the rate convention from the interest actually earned

This model uses nominal annual rates divided by twelve. Interest for a month is the opening balance multiplied by that monthly rate. The interest is credited at month-end, then the new deposit arrives. A contribution made at that point first earns interest in the following month.

For the first month, CAD 10,000 at 5% divided by twelve earns approximately CAD 41.67. The opening balance, credited interest and CAD 500 deposit then become the next month’s starting balance. The example does not pay 5% of principal after three months or treat every new deposit as if it had arrived at the beginning.

Monthly crediting also means an annual nominal rate and an effective annual yield are different concepts. If 5% nominal remained unchanged for twelve monthly periods, its effective yield would be (1 + 0.05 ÷ 12)12 − 1. The default promotion ends sooner, so that full-year constant-rate expression does not describe the selected account.

03

Compare the same principal and saving effort

At the end of twelve months, each account has received CAD 16,000 of principal: the initial CAD 10,000 plus twelve CAD 500 deposits. That principal is not interest. The cumulative-interest chart removes contributions so the difference in account earnings is visible even when both total balances are increasing.

Under the defaults, the introductory account earns about CAD 285.86 in interest over the year. The constant-rate account earns about CAD 387.35. The introductory account therefore finishes about CAD 101.49 behind, despite its higher opening rate.

The result depends on the selected dates, rates and deposits. It does not establish that introductory accounts are generally inferior. Extending the high-rate period or increasing the later rate can change the comparison. Holding the contributions identical prevents a different amount of household saving from being mistaken for an account-performance advantage.

04

A rate advantage is worth more when more money is present

Set monthly deposits to zero to isolate the initial CAD 10,000. The default introductory schedule earns about CAD 240.00, while the constant 3% account earns about CAD 304.16. Restoring monthly deposits changes the interest difference because later contributions mostly encounter the lower post-promotion rate.

A simple arithmetic average of the two rates can be informative about their time weights, but it does not by itself calculate interest when balances change and interest compounds. Each month has its own opening balance. The recurrence applies the rate to that amount before crediting the contribution.

The stacked endpoint bars reconcile the two ending balances into contributed principal and retained interest. They also show why a larger account statement is not automatically evidence of a superior rate: a growing balance can mostly reflect new money you supplied. Keep a contribution ledger beside any interest comparison, especially when transfers or withdrawals are uneven.

05

Use the matrix to test the part of the offer that may be overlooked

The matrix changes introductory duration and the ongoing rate, then compares cumulative interest with the selected constant-rate account. Its row labels identify the whole number of introductory months. A zero-month row starts immediately at the later rate; it does not create a high-rate payment at time zero.

Signed dollar amounts show introductory-account interest minus comparison-account interest. A positive cell is an advantage within those assumptions; a negative cell is a shortfall. If a row’s introductory duration extends beyond the selected horizon, only the months inside that horizon are used.

Try a six-month holding period and then a twenty-four-month period. A short promotion can have a different influence when the money remains much longer. The matrix does not assign a probability to future rates, assume an account will retain its entered ongoing rate in reality or recommend switching based on one shaded cell.

06

Reconcile the real offer before making a transfer

  1. Record the exact introductory start and end dates.
  2. Check whether the quoted rate is the total rate or a bonus added to a base rate.
  3. Identify qualifying balances, caps and account or transaction conditions.
  4. Check the later rate, fees and transfer timing.
  5. Compare interest using the same deposits, withdrawals and holding period.
  6. Review the account when the introduction expires.

Actual savings accounts may calculate interest daily, credit it monthly and apply different rules to parts of the balance. This simplified monthly example excludes those details, taxes, fees, withdrawals and transfer gaps. It also makes no deposit-insurance assessment. Use the actual agreement and dates to reconstruct a real offer; the lesson here is to keep the headline, expiry, balance calendar and earned dollars in the same comparison.
